Key Takeaways Revisions remain critical through rising investment and narrative whirlwinds of "GenAI risk and ROIC question marks". GOOGL delivered with all major revenue lines beating and forward growth visibility increasing. GOOGL rev ests beat across the board, but Google Cloud is the standout (ests up 9%/13% in '26/'27) as '26/'27 EPS rises by 7%/9% even thru higher opex. META's revenue estimates were tactically disappointing but stepping back don’t change much. But opex/capex are rising and investment ROIC in less certain MSL. We are OW GOOGL/META and detail key catalysts – GOOGL: Gemini 3 launch; META: Llama reasoning/next model launch – that will determine relative multiples. Revisions Trump Narratives: As shown in Exhibit 1 , GOOGL and META have a multitude of improving GenAI adoption signals, product improvements and nextgeneration LLM-enabled capabilities. These are important and exciting for long-term growth opportunities at both companies and are also critical to showing the tip of the spear in GenAI ROIC we detailed here. But as discussed in What Matters at 3Q EPS and into '26?, we continue to believe upward revisions will be important to driving periodic stock performance (and multiple) in this whirlwind of “GenAI risks and ROIC question marks.” In effect, we think revisions and confidence in ROIC on GenAI investment will be important to determining stock performance and the relative multiples for GOOGL and META in ’26. Even more impressive, the Google Cloud backlog grew 46% q/q adding ~$49bn, reaching $155bn (we assume total GOOGL backlog of ~$157bn including other components not reflected in Google Cloud). We believe (based on our analysis of quarterly dollar growth in Exhibit 2 ) this includes OpenAI and META for the first time… and that those may have driven half of the growth. But the company is executing broadly, signing more $1bn+ deals YTD than in the past 2 years combined (see here for more on our bullish view on GCP). And this is also before Google Cloud is set to receive an incremental estimated $50-$80bn from its recently announced Anthropic contract (see here)… giving the market more confidence in more durable growth. Flowing in the new backlog, we raise our ‘26/27 GOOGL cloud segment revenue by 9%/13% … now modeling 44%/35% y/y growth (see Exhibit 3 ). Stronger top-line offsets higher investment as we raise our ‘26/’27 EPS by ~7%/9%. We raise our PT to $330 driven by higher EPS estimates and a higher target multiple (~25X on ’27 EPS vs ~22X previously) as we see GOOGL’s improving GenAI business lines and surging cloud business warranting a higher multiple going forward. As a read-across, these results will put more pressure on AWS to deliver as its current backlog (as of 2Q) is only $195bn… and we are modeling/hoping for 20%+ revenue growth in ’26.
What Matters Next for GOOGL? 1) Gemini 3 launch expected before year end and next-generation capabilities the company will showcase (reasoning, diffusion capabilities, agentic commerce, agentic travel) furthering its GenAI leadership. 2) Commercial consumer behavior will be important to monitor as ChatGPT ships improving agentic products aimed at dislodging GOOGL’s leading commercial position in the funnel.
META Revenue Guide Mildly Disappointing as Super Intelligence and Core Opex and Capex Rise. Lower ‘26/’27 EPS by 5%/4%. PT to $820, Remain OW: META’s 4Q revenue guide was disappointing (top end 1% below us), but the ad miss wasn’t as large as we acknowledge we mis-modeled quarterly hardware sales that in aggregate probably added ~1% to our 4Q estimates. So while our ad revenue numbers aren’t changing, they are not going up… which matters in this revision vs narrative-driven tape. This is particularly true as META’s opex and capex are both heading higher from investment in the super intelligence team and core products. To be clear, we don’t think anything is broken with META’s core platform improvements, believe the pipeline for improvements remains long... and key fundamentals remain very strong (time spent accelerating on Facebook and Instagram, US time spent on Facebook and Instagram growing double digits). The challenge in the near term is revisions and estimates heading lower as higher opex causes us to lower our ‘26/’27 EPS by 5%/4%. META’s multiple may also be pressured/capped due to rising investment in the super intelligence team (the largest driver of the y/y capex increase in ’26)… which causes more uncertainty around ROIC.
What Matters Next for META? 1) Llama Reasoning or next-generation models from the Super Intelligence team in ’26 will be critical. Raising GOOGL/META ’26 Capex by 28%/10%. Expect the importance of revenue revisions to stay high as capex investment rises again… with GOOGL and META both raising ’25 capex guidance. We raise our GOOGL/META ’26 capex by 28%/10%, now modeling $135bn/$115bn of capex in ’26. As shown below, with GOOGL/META/MSFT updated for earnings, we now model data center spend from the 6 largest players to reach $570bn/$664bn in ‘26/’27… with only upward bias from here (AMZN on deck next). As one offset, we were encouraged to learn that GOOGL/META both filed for the OBBBA benefits we have written about in How Large Could OBBBA Be for AMZN, META, and GOOGL? which helps to offset the ’26 capex increases.
Don’t fret the tax charge. It is mainly accounting based and cash taxes are expected to benefit significantly from the OBBBA: Certain provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) allow deductions in excess of those allowed under the previously existing Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax (CAMT). META’s cash taxes will decline meaningfully from bonus depreciation and R&D expensing provisions in the OBBBA, reducing taxable income under both the regular and minimum tax regimes. Because META’s taxable income is further reduced by amortization of previously capitalized R&D and foreign-derived deduction eligible income provisions in the OBBBA, which are excluded from the CAMT calculation, META expects to be subject to the CAMT. The company recorded a valuation allowance against its deferred tax assets to reflect uncertainty around the timing of those future deductions, resulting in a one-time, non-cash deferred tax charge this quarter. A valuation allowance does impact income, but does not impact future cash flows.
